You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Step 2. Evaluate monthly food costs (1 hour)
Step 3. Check local zoning laws for exotic pets (2 hours)

Step 5. Look up common breed health issues (2 hours)
Step 6. Research grooming requirements (1 hour)
Step 7. Discuss the idea with all household members (2 hours)

Step 59. Consider the impact on home cleanliness (2 days)
Step 60. Write a "Pros and Cons" list (1 hour)
Step 61. Join a social media group for pet owners (30 minutes)
Step 62. Set a maximum "buy-in" price limit (30 minutes)
Step 63. Research the best time of year to bring a pet home (2 hours)
Step 64. Look into pet-friendly rental options (3 hours)
Step 65. Determine the desired age of the pet (1 day)
Step 66. Assess the need for a dog walker (1 hour)
Step 67. Calculate the cost of flea and tick prevention (30 minutes)
Step 68. Map out the nearest 24-hour animal hospital (1 hour)
Step 69. Check the reliability of local pet supply delivery (1 hour)
Step 70. Look into pet-proofing supplies (2 hours)
Step 71. Think about how a pet fits into 5-year plans (3 days)
Step 72. Evaluate the "mess" potential of different species (2 hours)
Step 73. Look for a local pet groomer (1 hour)
Step 74. Research common behavioral issues (3 hours)
Step 75. Determine who will be the primary caregiver (1 hour)
Step 76. Analyze the emotional readiness of the family (2 days)
Step 77. Finalize the monthly budget (1 hour)
Step 78. Visit a pet supply store to see products (1 hour)
Step 79. Look up local pet ordinances (1 hour)
Step 80. Consider the impact on guests and visitors (1 hour)
Step 81. Conduct a "trial weekend" with a friend's pet (2 days)
Step 82. Calculate the cost of spaying or neutering (1 hour)
Step 83. Review your physical activity level (2 days)
Step 84. Research dietary requirements (2 hours)
Step 85. Check for local dog parks or trails (1 hour)
Step 86. Reflect on past pet ownership experiences (3 hours)
Step 87. Discuss the financial plan with a spouse (1 hour)
Step 88. Verify the availability of local pet services (1 hour)
Step 89. Plan for pet-proofing the living room (2 hours)
Step 90. Finalize the home preparation list (1 hour)
Step 91. Take an allergy test (2 days)
Step 92. Research microchipping costs (30 minutes)
Step 93. Consult a financial advisor about long-term costs (1 hour)
Step 94. Select a name for the potential pet (30 minutes)
Step 95. Research the cost of training equipment (1 hour)
Step 96. Make the final "Go/No-Go" decision (1 hour)
Step 97. Check for upcoming adoption events (1 hour)
Step 98. Watch documentaries on animal care (3 hours)
Step 99. Sign a commitment pledge to the family (15 minutes)
Step 100. Review the impact on travel plans (1 day)
